This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

candidates: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:68 - `sed -i ''` only works with BSD/macOS sed and fails on Linux.. GNU sed reads `-i ''` as in-place editing with the empty string as the script. It then treats the `s|...|` expression as a file name and exits with an error, so on Linux `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is never updated when the key already exists. The script still prints "✅ Updated" because the sed exit status is never checked. Fix: write to a temp file and move it into place, or detect the platform and choose `sed -i` or `sed -i ''`.

Changing how `dev:cron` runs (`npx tsx` instead of `ts-node`) is unrelated. `npx` may also download tsx at run time if it is not installed. Move this to its own change or explain why it is needed.

packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:9 - Existing cache rows get the migration time as `updatedAt`, so old caches look freshly updated.. `DEFAULT NOW()` sets every existing `CalendarCache` row to the time the migration runs. The new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` / `cacheUpdatedAt` UI will then report every old or stale cache as updated at deploy time, until each row is written again. That is wrong status information, and it is what users rely on when deciding whether to delete the cache. A better backfill for existing rows is a value that reflects their real age, such as `"expiresAt" - interval '<cache TTL>'`, or NULL with a nullable column. Then the default can apply only to new rows.

scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:5 - ENV_FILE is resolved against the current directory, not the script's location.. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` depends on where the script is run from. Run from the repo root (`./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`), it creates or edits a `.env` in the folder above the repository, and the app never sees the webhook URL. Resolve it from the script's directory instead, for example `ENV_FILE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)/.env"`.

packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:89 - The cache timestamp is always formatted with the "en-US" locale.. The date ignores the user's locale and time format, so non-US users see dates like MM/DD/YY next to otherwise localised text. Use the locale from `useLocale()` (`i18n.language`) when building the formatter.

scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:17 - Failures exit with status 0.. `cleanup` always runs `exit 0`, including the rate-limit path and the "Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL" path. Callers and CI see these failures as success. Pass an exit code to `cleanup` and use a non-zero code on the error paths.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:24 - Access denial throws a plain Error, which tRPC reports as a 500.. Passing a credential the user does not own throws a generic `Error`. tRPC turns this into INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN, so it is logged as a server fault. Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` instead.
